Technology Hardware Workers Walk Out, Disrupting Cayman Islands Supply Chain

A major walkout by workers in the Technology Hardware sector has entered its third day in the Cayman Islands, causing significant disruptions to local supply chains and manufacturing operations. The industrial action, organized by the Cayman Information Technology Workers Union (CITWU), began Monday morning after negotiations over pay and working conditions with several industry employers—including IslandTech Components and BlueWave Devices—stalled late last week.

According to CITWU spokesperson Marcia Ebanks, over 400 workers across George Town and Bodden Town have joined the walkout. “Management’s refusal to address our concerns over overtime compensation and workplace safety left us with no choice,” Ebanks said at a press briefing Tuesday. “We are calling for fair wages and improved conditions for everyone in the sector.”

The impact has been immediate and far-reaching for local technology hardware producers and distributors. IslandTech Components confirmed that assembly lines at its main facility have been at a standstill since Monday, affecting the output of circuit boards and related components. “We are working to minimize disruption for our clients, but with the majority of our production staff participating in the walkout, our operations are severely limited,” said company representative Julian Carter.

BlueWave Devices, which specializes in networking hardware, reported shipment delays and warned customers of possible backorders. “We urge all parties to return to the negotiating table as soon as possible,” said BlueWave’s managing director, Patricia Lin.

Industry analysts estimate that the strike is costing the sector upwards of CI$120,000 per day in lost productivity and delayed orders. “This is a significant event for a sector that is crucial to both local businesses and regional exports,” noted Samuel Bodden, a technology industry consultant.

Negotiations between CITWU and employers are set to resume Wednesday, but as of Tuesday evening, no agreement had been reached and the walkout continues.
